privileged-container-agents.name: organizations/550178366891/sources/3913548688797809695/locations/global/findings/b54fa158d3244cdf9b6ffeacefaa9ec6
privileged-container-agents.category: Privilege Escalation: Launch of privileged Kubernetes container
privileged-container-agents.description:
A potentially malicious actor created a Pod that contains privileged containers (`privileged` field set to `true`) or containers with privilege escalation capabilities (`allowPrivilegeEscalation` field set to `true`).

Privileged containers allow nearly unrestricted host access. They share namespaces with the host, and lack control group, seccomp, AppArmor, and capability restrictions.

Containers with privilege escalation capabilities allow a process created within the container to execute a set-user-id, set-group-id, or file capability executable to gain the privileges specified by the executable. The lack of preventive security control increases the risk of container escape.

**Recommended action**

1. Confirm that the container created requires access to host resources and kernel capabilities.
1. Determine whether there are other signs of malicious activity by the principal in the logs.
1. If the principal email isn't a service account, contact the owner of the account to confirm whether the legitimate owner conducted the action.
1. If the principal email is a service account (IAM or Kubernetes), identify the source of the action to determine its legitimacy.

[More details](https://cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/findings/threats/gke-control-plane-launch-privileged-container)

intranode-visibility.description: Enabling intranode visibility makes your intranode Pod-to-Pod traffic visible to the networking fabric. With this feature, you can use VPC flow logging or other VPC features to monitor or control intranode traffic. To get logs, you need to enable VPC flow logs in the selected subnetwork.

sourceProperties.Recommendation: Go to https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/clusters/details/europe-north1-a/k8-lab/details?project=project-69726555-c4de-48de-a69. In the "Networking" section, click on the edit icon in the "Intranode visibility" row. In the dialog that appears, enable the feature and then click "SAVE CHANGES". Note that a cluster cannot be modified while it is reconfiguring itself.
sourceProperties.ExceptionInstructions: Add the security mark "allow_intranode_visibility_disabled" to the asset with a value of "true" to prevent this finding from being activated again.

exposed-forwarding-rule.description: A  service was found to be externally reachable from the public internet via port 443. This exposure was confirmed by a behavior-based scan and may allow unauthorized access if not properly secured.
exposed-forwarding-rule.name: organizations/550178366891/sources/14154167499029398336/locations/global/findings/2760353128242953903
exposed-forwarding-rule.nextSteps:
* __Apply WAF and access controls__: Use the provided network path insights to review the specific forwarding rules, backend services, and current security policies. Attach a [Cloud Armor security policy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/configure-security-policies#update-policies) to the backend service to restrict access. Additionally, ensure the backend instances (VMs or GKE nodes) are shielded by VPC firewall rules that *only* allow ingress from the load balancer's proxy-only subnets or Google Front End (GFE) IP ranges, preventing direct internet bypass.
* __Monitor and audit traffic__: Enable [logging](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs) and [threat detection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/overview-threats) for suspicious activity. Potential exploitation has been observed leading to cloud credential harvesting and cryptocurrency mining.

__Note__: Follow your organization’s patching and change management processes to minimize operational impact.
[Learn more about validating External Exposure findings](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/detect-external-exposure).
